This year I'll plant like I always do — wheat in winter, maize after the wheat comes off, and I keep a small piece for cotton because the price has been alright and I know that plot. Out of my 13.1 mu, I'll put 10 mu on the wheat-maize rotation and the other 3.1 mu on cotton. My land sits near the well so water isn't my biggest worry, fertilizer cost is.

For wheat, last year I used about two bags of compound fertilizer (45% NPK) as base and one bag of urea topdress at jointing. That works out to roughly 16 kg nitrogen, 8 kg phosphorus, 6 kg potassium per mu. I got around 500 kg/mu, which is normal for our village. I'll do the same — the neighbor who cut back last year lost some yield and I won't take that chance. Irrigation three times: before winter, at jointing, and at grain filling. I spray once for aphids and once for rust, so two sprays. I plough before sowing because the stubble needs turning in.

For summer maize after wheat, I use Zhengdan 958 or a similar hybrid — everyone around here does. I'll no-till drill right into the wheat stubble, save time and diesel. About 18 kg N, 5 kg P, 5 kg K per mu, mostly urea sidedressed at the big trumpet stage. One irrigation usually, maybe two if July is dry. Two pesticide sprays — one for armyworm, one for corn borer. Target 580 kg/mu.

Cotton is more work. I use an improved Bt variety so the bollworm pressure is lower, but I still spray maybe 6-7 times for aphids, mites, and late bollworm. I rotary till, put 13 kg N, 7 kg P, 9 kg K per mu, and irrigate 4 times. I expect 270 kg/mu seed cotton — that's what I got last two years.
